metadata.title: Free AI in 2026: What You Actually Get
metadata.subtitle: Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, free APIs, and local models — matched to the constraint that matters
metadata.purpose: Teach the constraint-first framework: there is no universally best free AI service. The practical move is to identify the binding constraint — depth, research, coding, pipeline cost, or privacy — and match the tool to it. Every specific limit is volatile; the framework is durable.
metadata.source: pasted-text.txt — research compilation on free AI tiers (unresolved <cite> markers; SEO-warning flagged by source itself); first-party vendor docs required for volatile specifics
metadata.notes: Kokoro am_onyx, free (IN-FOR-BEAR LAW). GATE P before any ElevenLabs swap. Deep-explainer: 5 acts, 30 body beats, VOX 27% / MANIM 27% / REMOTION 30% / CARD 17%. Vox runs R1 (B24–B25) R2 (B29–B30). SOURCING HONESTY: specific version numbers, rate-limit figures, and caps are labeled UNCONFIRMED on screen (verify at vendor console). Beat mix histogram: WARN on VOX 27% (target 20–25%, within 15–30% acceptable). FACTCHECK.md documents every volatile claim. Never publish.

beats.narration_text: Here's the full answer up front. There is no universally best free AI. Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, free APIs, and local models trade off depth, speed, privacy, and reliability in ways that don't rank cleanly. And every specific limit you find online is already stale. The practical move: know your constraint first, then match the tool to it.

beats.act: ACT I — Free Is Not One Thing
beats.narration_text: Free means at least three different things. Free chat access: time-limited, message-capped, rate-throttled. Free API tokens: often rate-limited to research-grade throughput only. And free as in no-cost-at-all: local models on your hardware, permanent, private, zero rate limits.

beats.act: ACT I — Free Is Not One Thing
beats.narration_text: Here's the framework before the detail. Five constraints that route to different answers: depth and long documents, research synthesis, coding access, free pipeline or API work, and privacy. This video covers each in order. Hold onto the one that's most true for your work — that's the one that matters.

beats.act: ACT I — Free Is Not One Thing
beats.narration_text: Every specific limit in this video is already stale before it's published. All three major platforms changed their default models, message caps, or features multiple times in a single year. Treat any specific number as a lead, not a contract — and verify before you build on it.

beats.narration_text: Gemini's free tier leads on one thing: Deep Research is included. Multi-source synthesized reports — the feature Claude gates behind paid. beats.narration_text: Context window matters when you're working with long documents — a research paper, a contract, a lecture transcript. Claude's free tier reportedly carries the full 200K window. One source puts Gemini's free chat tier at a smaller ceiling. That difference is real if your work involves long documents — and worth verifying against the current console before you depend on it.

beats.narration_text: ChatGPT's free tier is the hardest to characterize precisely. The default model name has changed multiple times in a single year. Sources from the same period disagree. The consistent pattern: a capable base model, around ten messages every five hours before fallback to a lighter version, and ads for US users.

beats.act: ACT III — APIs Change the Math
beats.narration_text: Consumer chat and API access are different tiers. Chat limits apply to you, using the interface. API limits apply to your code calling the underlying model. Google AI Studio's free API tier gives developer-grade rate limits, multimodal input, and long-context support on some models.

beats.act: ACT III — APIs Change the Math
beats.narration_text: Groq provides free API access to open-weight models — sub-200 millisecond time to first token, compatible with the OpenAI SDK, with daily request quotas in the tens of thousands. That's the call for pipeline steps that need speed over frontier quality: routing, tagging, fast extraction.

beats.act: ACT III — APIs Change the Math
beats.narration_text: Some developers stack multiple free tiers deliberately: Claude chat for analysis and writing, Gemini AI Studio for long context, Groq for speed, OpenRouter for variety. Effectively unlimited frontier-class access at zero monthly spend. The cost: juggling accounts and accepting no single provider is infrastructure-grade reliable.

beats.act: ACT III — APIs Change the Math
beats.narration_text: Which surfaces the reliability problem. Every free tier reserves the right to rate-limit, throttle, or cut off access without notice. A pipeline built on free tiers is an experiment. When it breaks, you're waiting on a vendor decision — not debugging your own code.

beats.act: ACT IV — Local Changes the Bargain
beats.narration_text: Local models change the deal. You own the compute: no rate limits, no message caps, no training-data exposure, no vendor deprecating the model under you. The tradeoff: setup, hardware requirements, and a capability ceiling below current frontier cloud models.

beats.act: ACT IV — Local Changes the Bargain
beats.narration_text: What runs on a modern laptop: small models at four to eight gigabytes handle fast extraction and summarization. The mid-size range at sixteen gigabytes is capable but not frontier. Larger models need thirty-two to sixty-four gigabytes. On Apple Silicon, recent runtime updates roughly doubled local decode speed — but the faster path requires thirty-two gigabytes of unified memory or more.

beats.act: ACT IV — Local Changes the Bargain
beats.narration_text: The MIT-licensed DeepSeek R1 family spans the whole size range and shows its reasoning steps — chain-of-thought visible in the output. That's the model family worth knowing about at this tier. But single-source performance figures are leads, not facts: any benchmark claim needs a model, a runtime, a hardware spec, and a reproducible test.

beats.act: ACT IV — Local Changes the Bargain
beats.narration_text: The privacy case for local is simple. Every cloud service — even a paid one — is governed by a data policy you don't control. Medical notes, unreleased research, privileged communications: there are categories of work where having the model on your own hardware is the only acceptable answer.

beats.act: ACT IV — Local Changes the Bargain
beats.narration_text: Local isn't about capability. It's about control. The feature no cloud tier can match: your data never leaves your machine. That's not an edge case for specialized workflows. That's the design.

beats.narration_text: Here's the routing matrix — the framework from Act I, walked through with current cases. Long documents: Claude or Gemini free, each offering meaningful context. Research synthesis at zero cost: Gemini Deep Research, the only tier including that free. Coding access: ChatGPT Codex reportedly free-tier; Claude Code is paid. Pipeline cost: stack Groq, Gemini AI Studio, OpenRouter. Privacy: local only.

beats.narration_text: Add one more constraint: reliability. If a process depends on the model being there at 2am or during a launch, free tiers are not the answer. Free is for experimentation and personal work. The moment something critical runs on a free tier, you need to account for that explicitly.

beats.narration_text: The meta-principle: start with the constraint, not the tool. Depth first? Look at Claude or Gemini free. Speed first? Groq. Privacy first? Local. Versatility through one key? OpenRouter. The tool is the answer. The constraint is the question.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. No universal winner — you're matching a constraint, not picking a champion. For long documents: Claude or Gemini free give you meaningful context windows. Research synthesis at zero cost: Gemini Deep Research is the only tier giving that away free right now. For coding access: ChatGPT's Codex reportedly has a free-tier opening; Claude Code is paid. Free API pipelines: stack Groq for speed, Gemini AI Studio for long context, OpenRouter for variety. For privacy: local model only — no cloud tier competes. And for reliability: none of these are infrastructure. Verify the limits before you depend on them.
